analogies: Taking meeting notes instead of recording the whole meeting — shorter, but you can only find what the note-taker wrote down.
definition: Context compaction is how a long-running agent keeps working for hours without hitting its memory limit. A model can only consider a fixed amount of text at once — the context window. As an agent works, that window fills up with tool results, web pages, and chat history. Compaction kicks in near the limit: the agent (or the platform running it) summarizes the older history into a compact note — decisions made, facts learned, current state — and keeps going from the summary instead of the full log. OpenAI's Agents API does this automatically, so developers don't write their own compaction logic.

edges.label: works around its limit
edges.note: Compaction exists because the context window is finite and long agent sessions fill it.

edges.label: lets loops run for hours
edges.note: Without compaction, an agentic loop would grind to a halt once its memory filled up.

edges.label: lowers the bill
edges.note: Replacing raw history with a short summary cuts the tokens re-read every turn.

example.body: You ask an agent to compare five project-management tools for your team. Two hours in it has visited dozens of pages and its memory is nearly full, so it compacts: “Asana: $10.99/user, Gantt charts on the Business tier, marketing liked it; Monday: $8/user but no time tracking…” The reasoning continues from the summary, not the raw pages. If the summary dropped the caveat that Monday's price requires annual billing, the final report is wrong in a way that looks confident — which is exactly why what the summary keeps matters.
example.title: The six-hour research task

footnotes.body: Per OpenAI's Agents API documentation, the runtime “automatically compacts earlier context as a session nears its limit” and preserves the model's prompt cache where possible. Multi-agent runs get an extra benefit: each sub-agent keeps its own context, so the main agent only receives their summaries — compaction by architecture.
footnotes.label: For the technical reader

name: Context Compaction
tagline: How long-running agents shrink old conversation history into summaries so they don't run out of memory.
whyItMatters: Always-on agents like dots only work if they can run for hours without forgetting what they're doing or crashing into a limit. Compaction is the quiet technique that makes long autonomous runs practical — and a place where things go subtly wrong, because whatever the summary drops is gone for good.
